records.summary: Cape Percar is the western peninsula wrapping Topal Bay, Soulrest's hinterland of burned mines, quarries, timber camps and coastal villages. Drier and hillier than the washes east of it, it carries the burn scar of the Great Burn.
records.landform: A forested peninsula of low hills and coastal flats, cut by tidal creeks, with mines in the hills and a burn-scarred strip.
records.biome: Coastal swamp forest and mangrove, with drier red-gum hills
records.climate: Warm, humid, with sea breezes and mist from the Sea of Mists; wet season floods the creeks.

notes.text: The cape is the peninsula behind Soulrest. It holds the old Imperial mines and timber concessions, a few villages and a burn scar.

sources.title: Cape Percar region, its places on the map and the Soulrest dossier

notes.text: Gold and timber concessions ran here until the tribes burned them in 3E 427; the Great Burn's underground network reached the cape in 1E 2828.

sources.title: Cape Percar region, its places on the map and the Soulrest dossier

notes.text: Villages and licensed camps work timber and stone under Soulrest's council; the mines stand derelict; Banujha mine-burners keep watch posts at its edges.

sources.title: Cape Percar region, its places on the map and the Soulrest dossier

notes.text: Umber coast folk: Argonians, Khajiit coasters and Imperial-descended families, with Banujha watchers and a Naka-Desh river station at the edges.

sources.title: Cape Percar region, its places on the map and the Soulrest dossier

notes.text: Timber, stone, fish and salt for Soulrest; the mines are derelict.

sources.title: Cape Percar region, its places on the map and the Soulrest dossier

notes.text: Sithis and the Hist through inland trees; a few Nine shrines of Imperial families.

sources.title: Cape Percar region, its places on the map and the Soulrest dossier

notes.text: Red-gum hills, black burn-scars, grey-stone Imperial ruins and stilt villages on the coast.

sources.title: Cape Percar region, its places on the map and the Soulrest dossier

notes.text: Highwaymen, burn-gas, flooded mines and hostile tribes; roads and towns are safer.

sources.title: Cape Percar region, its places on the map and the Soulrest dossier

notes.text: Low hills up to about 45 m behind the coast, flat sandy shores, salt creeks and mangrove edges.

sources.title: Cape Percar region, its places on the map and the Soulrest dossier

notes.text: Red gum, mangrove, wading birds, sea-drakes at the shore; the burn-scar is bare.

sources.title: Cape Percar region, its places on the map and the Soulrest dossier

notes.text: Humid and warm; sea mist on the south coast; rain is frequent and the low creeks stand full.

records.summary: The Tulmek Washes are the drowned lowland between Soulrest's cape and the Lilmoth delta, centred on Blackrose's lake and its three rivers. A mosaic of channels, islands and ruins, it is the hinge of the south.
records.landform: Flat flooded lowland of river channels, lakes, mud islands and small dry rises, with the Blackrose lake at its heart.
records.climate: Hot, wet and still; annual flood cycle with boardwalk decks above wet-season level.

notes.text: The washes are the wet country around Blackrose where three rivers converge; Bramman's river runs out to Topal Bay.

sources.title: Tulmek Washes region, the places between Soulrest and the Blackrose lakes

notes.text: Lilmothiit lands, then Kothringi towns, then the Imperial prison and city, then Red Bramman's kingdom; the 4E 48 catastrophe emptied Murkmire to the south-east.

sources.title: Tulmek Washes region, the places between Soulrest and the Blackrose lakes

notes.text: Blackrose city holds the lake; the Rose is held by the Blackguards' heirs; oxblood towns, rose delta villages and umber road towns sit around them.

sources.title: Tulmek Washes region, the places between Soulrest and the Blackrose lakes

notes.text: Olive lake-folk, oxblood Chime-Keepers, rose delta farmers, umber carters, the Blackguards' heirs and Naga.

sources.title: Tulmek Washes region, the places between Soulrest and the Blackrose lakes

notes.text: Tolls at the confluence, fish, reeds, rice, chimes, smuggling.

sources.title: Tulmek Washes region, the places between Soulrest and the Blackrose lakes

notes.text: Drowned Hist at Blackrose, Sithis and a regard for Z'en and Dibella at Toklea.

sources.title: Tulmek Washes region, the places between Soulrest and the Blackrose lakes

notes.text: Brown water, reed beds, stilt towns, boardwalks, drowned domes and mist.

sources.title: Tulmek Washes region, the places between Soulrest and the Blackrose lakes

notes.text: Crocodilians, gar, deep channels, bandits and the Rose; the deep washes are dangerous.

sources.title: Tulmek Washes region, the places between Soulrest and the Blackrose lakes

notes.text: Dead-flat lowland of standing water with tiny rises; channels braid round low islands of reed and mud.

sources.title: Tulmek Washes region, the places between Soulrest and the Blackrose lakes

notes.text: Reeds, mangroves, cypress, gar, crocodilians, herons; sea-drakes at the south shore.

sources.title: Tulmek Washes region, the places between Soulrest and the Blackrose lakes

notes.text: The washes are hot, humid and still; rain falls most days and the water stands across the whole lowland between the cape and the delta.

records.summary: The Sea of Mists is the Southern Sea off Black Marsh's south coast, between Cape Percar and the Lilmoth coast, held under a low mist most mornings. Wrecks, small islands and a lighthouse mark it.
records.landform: Shallow shelf sea with sandbars and low islets off a drowned coast.
records.climate: Warm, humid, with sea mist on most mornings and storms in the wet season.

notes.text: The Sea of Mists is the part of the Southern Sea south of Cape Percar, a grey-green shelf sea off Black Marsh's south coast.

sources.title: Sea of Mists region, the water south of Cape Percar and the Tulmek Washes

notes.text: Pirates of the Southern Sea avoid attention. Many of its seafarers are Khajiit. Legend says Murkmire once extended further south and was swallowed by the sea.

sources.title: Sea of Mists region, the water south of Cape Percar and the Tulmek Washes

notes.text: Fishing boats and small coasters ply it, with salvagers at the wrecks and smugglers' landings.

sources.title: Sea of Mists region, the water south of Cape Percar and the Tulmek Washes

notes.text: Argonian fishers, Khajiit coasters and a few Bosmer seafarers work the sea's boats and landings along the coast.

sources.title: Sea of Mists region, the water south of Cape Percar and the Tulmek Washes

notes.text: The sea's coast lives on fishing, wreck salvage, coastal freight and smuggling in small boats.

sources.title: Sea of Mists region, the water south of Cape Percar and the Tulmek Washes

notes.text: Sailors hold rites for the drowned, and Argonian boats carry a Sithis token on the stem.

sources.title: Sea of Mists region, the water south of Cape Percar and the Tulmek Washes

notes.text: Grey-green water, mist banks, low islets and mangrove edges.

sources.title: Sea of Mists region, the water south of Cape Percar and the Tulmek Washes

notes.text: Sea-drakes, shoals, pirates and sudden fog threaten every boat that leaves the shore.

sources.title: Sea of Mists region, the water south of Cape Percar and the Tulmek Washes

notes.text: The sea is a shelf about 35 m deep, scattered with sandbars and low islets.

sources.title: Sea of Mists region, the water south of Cape Percar and the Tulmek Washes

notes.text: Sea-drakes, fat sleeper, longlure eelfin, spotted seatrout, seabirds.

sources.title: Sea of Mists region, the water south of Cape Percar and the Tulmek Washes

notes.text: The Sea of Mists is warm and humid with mist most mornings; rain and thunderstorms are common.
